rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's fifteen builder trees go (magnolias, jacarandas and a ficus along the back fences, a jacaranda 3 m from a house front, a few in the yards inside the wrought-iron fence); five come back on their own spots, about one for every two houses: on the open lot corner, in two yards inside the iron fence, and two on the north back fence row 51 m apart.

trees.why: the open lot corner inside the wrought-iron fence, 32 m from the walls: a full magnolia
the yard north of it, 12 m from the house, 31 m from the magnolia
the middle yard inside the same fence, 13.5 m from the house
the north back fence row's east end, 7 m from the house: one of its two trees kept
the same row 51 m west, 6.5 m from the house: its second tree
